text:
[BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) learns masked-item reconstruction using left and right context; next-item inference instead predicts an appended MASK without right context. Thus, strong interior reconstruction can coexist with weak next-item ranking. [DualRec (2022)](https://www.atailab.cn/seminar2022Fall/pdf/2022_CIKM_Disentangling%20Past-Future%20Modeling%20in%20Sequential%20Recommendation%20via%20Dual%20Networks.pdf) explicitly identifies this context discrepancy. Its dual-network solution falls outside the present single-model constraint, but its diagnosis motivates measuring the gap directly.

Proposed probe, rather than a published standardized metric: select matched targets within public training histories; compare interior MASK reconstruction against prefix-only appended-MASK prediction using identical targets and candidate sets. Report paired changes in target negative log-likelihood, rank and HR@10, stratified by prefix length and available right-context length. Removing right context also changes target position under left padding; add an attention-masked, position-preserving control to distinguish context dependence from positional effects. Always hide the target with reserved MASK; appended inference reads the final nonpadding position, never count−1.

For prefix-only inputs, compare recent-k removal against equal-sized older-item removal, then shuffle history while preserving its item multiset; additionally shuffle older items while fixing the recent suffix. Measure paired ranking changes and uncertainty across users. [Positional encoding research (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.10436) distinguishes positional relations from temporal context; [CAPE (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09027) further motivates testing position representations. A large reconstruction gap suggests testing more terminal-mask supervision within the same BERT4Rec model; shuffle sensitivity motivates positional ablations. These are hypotheses: perturbations measure model dependence, not causal user preferences.
